coordinate_system.orientation_notes: Use the front-view convention: global Z follows the central bore axis, with X and Y in the front-view plane and viewing direction -Z. Section A-A describes the longitudinal axis as its local X and the radial direction as local Y; normalize those view-local axes to this global convention. Datum A establishes the radial origin, but an axial zero is not specified.

features.name: Central bore Ø22
features.description: Central cylindrical bore of nominal diameter 22.00 mm, designated as Datum A.

geometry.position_description: Centred on the primary axis of rotation

features.name: Opposing end faces (Datum B)
features.description: Two parallel planar end faces defining the overall length of the part and establishing Datum B.

relationships.detail: The cylindrical ends and central bore share the part's axis of revolution.
The central boss and central bore share the part's axis of revolution.
The end cylinders and central boss lie on the common section centerline.
The position control on the cylindrical ends references Datum A, established by the central bore.
The position control on the central boss references Datum A, established by the central bore.
The opposing planar end faces are geometrically normal to the longitudinal bore axis; this edge does not assert a perpendicularity tolerance.
The opposing end faces bound the outer ends of the cylindrical end steps.
The convex shoulder blends join the central boss outer surface at its shoulder boundaries.
The concave neck fillets join the cylindrical end steps to the shoulder transitions.

datums.description: Internal cylindrical surface of the central bore.
Opposing outer end faces of the component.

datum_scheme.datum_hierarchy_notes: A is the sole datum referenced in both position-control frames. B is defined on the opposing end faces, but no supplied feature-control frame establishes an A–B hierarchy. The intended construction of Datum B requires clarification; neither an individual end face nor a derived median plane has been selected.

feature_graph.part_notes: Material: ASTM A311 CLASS A 1035-1144. Material standard: ASTM A311. Scale: 1:1. General tolerance: ASME Y14.5-2009. Projection: third angle. Heat treatment: none specified. TOLERANCE: METRIC DIMENSIONS & TOLERANCES GOVERN THE DESIGN. ENGLISH DIMENSIONS IF INCLUDED ARE FOR INFORMATION PURPOSES ONLY.. Testing: CRUSH TEST per PS-122.5 (100kN, 200kN, 0.375mm).

assumptions.text: All supplied feature observations remain singletons. Although Section A-A notes the central through-bore, its feature list contains no bore observation that can legitimately be grouped with front_view:F1; no synthetic member or field override was created.
The explicit through-bore statement in the Section A-A extraction notes resolves the front-view uncertainty about through versus blind condition, so no bore-depth clarification is raised.

The paired end faces, end cylinders, convex shoulder radii, and concave neck fillets retain their supplied multiplicities. No individually identified counterparts exist, so no aggregate identity groups are required.
The convex shoulder radii and concave neck fillets remain distinct features despite their matching radius callouts, because their surface roles and locations differ.

The differing axial letters in the two coordinate notes are treated as view-local conventions. Global Z is selected from the front-view bore-axis convention rather than treating the section's local X as a different physical axis.
Datum B remains attached to the supplied paired-end-face observation pending C01. No particular end face or median plane is silently substituted.
Datum B is intended as the derived median plane of the opposing end faces, as both end faces are identically identified with Datum B annotations across the overall length dimension.
